**Finding submitted: deviation (Section 19, ¶p0133).**

Section 19 is drafted as a **no-hire**, not a non-solicit — it bars us and our affiliates from *hiring* "any employee of the other party" for the term plus one year. The first limb reaches all of the Vendor's employees (the "directly involved" qualifier attaches only to the second, ex-employee limb), and there is no carve-out for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches. No-hire provisions covering all Vendor personnel are walk-away territory under NOSOLICIT, so the clause fails the fallback on material terms.

The validated redline (ok:true) replaces it with a mutual non-solicit that: limits scope to personnel directly involved in the services; runs 12 months from the end of that involvement; and expressly permits hiring individuals who respond to general advertising or approach us unsolicited. This preserves the mutual protection the parties bargained for while removing the restriction on ordinary hiring.
